items.title: Mike Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2024
items.q: you listen to John Coltrane play, he’s using all kinds of substitutions on standards and chords

ctx.x: That particular song I mentioned, that Stones song, has a fairly basic chord progression. Do you feel that you’re more likely to play outside the changes on a song like that, that has less harmonic material than I guess — more than what — well maybe like a standard bebop with more changes.

I think the answer to that would be yes for me. I mean I think it’s easier — easier is not the right word — I think it lends itself to more harmonic experimentation if the bass of the chords, the harmonic movement of the chords, is simpler. It gives you I think a little bit more time to develop things in terms of playing outside the key centers. But that said of course you can listen to, you know pick whoever you want but you know you listen to John Coltrane play, he’s using all kinds of substitutions on…
Is there such a thing as wrong notes for you?
